title: Shape the demand curve

readouts.l: Simple rule: PED × % change in price

predict.q: PED is −0.5 along the whole curve. Price rises by 10%. By about how much does quantity demanded fall?

options.fb: That divides 10 by 0.5. PED = %ΔQd ÷ %ΔP, so %ΔQd = PED × %ΔP = −0.5 × 10 = −5%.
PED is a ratio of percentages: −0.5 means 0.5% for every 1% change in price, so 5% for 10%.

options.s: 0%: inelastic means quantity does not change
options.fb: 0% happens only when PED = 0 (perfectly inelastic). Inelastic means quantity responds less than in proportion.

task: Move the **PED** slider from 0 to −3 and watch the curve turn from vertical, through the unitary curve, towards flat.

target.do: Move the PED slider (try 0, −1 and −3), then press Check.

takeaway: PED tells you the % change in quantity for each 1% change in price.
